questions.question: On low bridges:

options.text: Height warnings must always be posted.
Height warnings must be posted at least twice.
Height warnings may be posted, but are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Height warnings may be posted, but are not required.
questions.explanation: Height warnings are sometimes posted on low bridges, but not always. If you are unsure whether your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, drive slowly.

questions.question: What is a shut-off valve?

options.text: A device that stops air from leaving an air brake system
An object connected to the spring brake system

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that stops air from leaving an air brake system
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. Always keep the rear shut-off valve closed to prevent air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle in front of you.
Avoid using tricks to help others pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, increase your following distance, avoid quick moves, and do not use tricks like flashing lights. Speeding up will only make the tailgater follow at a higher speed, increasing danger.

questions.question: What happens if you unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer?

options.text: The tow bar may fly up and cause injury.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tow bar may fly up and cause injury.
questions.explanation: Always pull the dolly out from under the rear trailer before unlocking the pintle hook. If you do not, the tow bar can fly up and cause serious injury.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, you should:

options.text: Push the accelerator to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves.
questions.explanation: To reduce the risk of tipping over with a trailer, steer gently and smoothly. Avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths.
questions.correctAnswerText: Truck rollovers
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered. Take corners slowly.

questions.question: A truck should be parked:

options.text: So that it must be backed up to leave the space.
So that it can be pulled forward to leave the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that it can be pulled forward to leave the space.
questions.explanation: You cannot see everything behind you, so backing is dangerous and should be avoided. Choose parking spaces where you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: Both systems in a dual air brake system share:
questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor.
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor fails, neither system will work properly.

questions.question: Combination vehicles are usually:

options.text: Easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.
More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more driving skill than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: Requires more driving skill
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle usually requires more skill than driving a single vehicle. Combination vehicles are longer and heavier than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: An axle brake system
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving, what should you do?

options.text: The vehicle should be running and in gear.
The engine should be turned off.
The check can be done from inside the vehicle.
The check can be done by looking at a reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: To check your lights, set the parking brake, turn off the engine, and remove the key. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out of the vehicle and check that all lights work properly.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail for one of two reasons. Which is one of them?

options.text: There is a loss of hydraulic pressure.
The brakes are used too much in one day.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a loss of hydraulic pressure.
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failures happen for two main reasons. First, brakes can fade if used too much on a downgrade. Second, there can be a loss of hydraulic pressure in the system. Well-maintained brakes rarely fail, but you should know what to do if they do.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: The air pressure has become too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure has become too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, how can a driver reduce speed?

options.text: Letting the truck run out of gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shifting into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes fail, shifting into a lower gear can help slow your vehicle down.

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do?

options.text: Is necessary to warm up parts of the engine.
Is encouraged to improve gas mileage.
Should be done on surfaces with poor traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause damage to the vehicle.

questions.question: Steering wheel play of more than ____ can make steering difficult.
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This equals about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel. More play than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: What about rims with welding repairs?

options.text: Are not safe to be used.
Are acceptable to be used on tires on the rear of a vehicle.
Are acceptable to be used only when carrying a heavy load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not safe to be used.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded should never be used.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is required to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. This helps a driver know if their brakes are beginning to fade.

questions.question: When starting an engine, what should happen?

options.text: Warning lights should turn on, then quickly turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should turn on, then quickly turn off.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should go out after a few seconds. If they do not turn off, something may be wrong with the vehicle.
